title: Quantum Walk-Based Graph Exploration for Drug Discovery
abstract: Drug discovery remains a complex and time-consuming process, largely constrained by the vastness of chemical space. Traditional methods often rely on high-throughput screening, which is both expensive and inefficient. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing quantum walks on graph representations of molecules to efficiently explore this chemical space. The core idea involves encoding molecular structures as graphs and leveraging the unique properties of quantum walks – specifically, their ability to simultaneously explore multiple paths – to accelerate the search for potential drug candidates. We formulate the problem as a quantum walk on a graph (G = (V, E)), where V represents the nodes (atoms) and E represents the edges (bonds) of the molecule. The walk is defined by a transition probability matrix P, which is derived from the molecular graph and specifies the likelihood of transitioning between neighboring nodes. The objective is to find the shortest path to a target node, representing a molecule with desired properties, using the quantum walk algorithm. We explore the theoretical possibilities and outline a computational framework. The potential of this approach to dramatically reduce the time and cost associated with drug discovery is highlighted.

title: Web-Based OBE Learning Assessment System with Rule-Based Student Profile Mapping
abstract: This study is motivated by the implementation of the Outcome-Based Education (OBE) curriculum in the Information Systems Study Program at the University of Bengkulu, which still faces operational challenges due to managing Graduate Learning Outcomes (PLO) and Course Learning Outcomes (CLO) through manual spreadsheet-based tracking. This localized workflow is prone to entry errors, lacks collaborative environments, and fails to systematically trace high-level structural insights from raw continuous academic marks. This research aims to design and develop a web-based automated evaluation ecosystem called Acapela that provides centralized tracking of PLO-CLO matrices, incorporates interactive diagram visualization components, and deploys a predictive analytics feature using a rule-based inference mechanism. The development uses a modified Research and Development (R&D) strategy incorporating qualitative methods via deep institutional observation and stakeholder interviews alongside quantitative validation using systematic User Acceptance Testing (UAT) evaluated via five-point Likert scales. The empirical testing demonstrates that the Acapela platform effectively manages centralized configurations, executes automated curriculum-linked score aggregations, maps multidimensional outputs via radar charts, and successfully resolves multi-criteria decision steps to yield student profile predictions classified into five granular performance bands. Software correctness was fully verified through automated black-box scenarios, while field utility metrics achieved an overall viability rate of 87.05% from operational user groups, denoting high feasibility for strategic deployment. Keywords: Academic analytics; Automated evaluation; Information systems curriculum; Outcome-Based Education; Web-based application.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric transformation optimization algorithm leveraging quantum computing principles, specifically focusing on quantum error correction and quantum computation. Traditional optimization techniques often struggle with complex geometric transformations, necessitating manual parameter tuning and limiting the algorithm's adaptability. This work proposes a quantum-enhanced approach that dynamically adjusts parameters based on quantum error correction, enabling a self-adaptive optimization process. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around quantum state manipulation to achieve precise and efficient geometric transformations. The paper details the proposed algorithm's architecture, explores its potential benefits, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its efficacy in a specific geometric transformation problem. The focus is on showcasing the advantages of quantum computation in addressing geometric optimization challenges.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre yet fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper investigates the application of quantum entanglement to enhance quantum computing capabilities and develops novel security protocols to safeguard quantum computations. The research highlights the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of existing quantum algorithms and addresses critical security challenges within the burgeoning field of quantum computing.

title: Adaptive Constraint-Driven Algorithm for Data Compression
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Constraint-Driven Algorithm for Data Compression, designed to optimize compression ratios by dynamically adjusting the constraint set used during compression. Traditional compression methods often employ fixed constraints, limiting the achievable compression efficiency. Our algorithm leverages a 'constraint curve' learned through analysis of the input data to intelligently modify the constraint set, resulting in significantly improved compression performance. The core mechanism involves a continuous learning process that refines the constraint set to maximize data representation. This approach offers a more flexible and adaptable solution compared to static constraint-based methods. We present a comprehensive evaluation demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness across various data types, achieving state-of-the-art compression ratios in several scenarios.

title: Title: Hierarchical Bayesian Graph Embedding for Complex Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a Hierarchical Bayesian Graph Embedding (HBGE) method to analyze complex networks. Complex networks often exhibit intricate relationships and require representations that accurately capture structural properties. Traditional graph embedding techniques, while useful, can struggle with large-scale data and the discovery of subtle patterns. This research introduces a novel HBGE framework that leverages Bayesian hierarchical Bayesian modeling to automatically generate hierarchical graphs, offering a more robust and scalable approach to network analysis. The method aims to improve representation quality and facilitate the identification of complex network structures. The core mechanism involves iteratively constructing the graph, incorporating node features and relationships, and employing Bayesian inference to refine the graph structure. This paper will detail the theoretical framework, implementation details, and experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of the HBGE method in extracting meaningful insights from complex networks.

This represents a significant advancement in the field, addressing a critical challenge in quantum simulation – the complexities of parameter calibration. The system's design emphasizes adaptability and precision, potentially unlocking new capabilities for exploring the behavior of quantum systems.

abstract: This paper explores the utilization of quantum tunneling to create a dynamic, adaptive metric mapping, offering a novel approach to geometric analysis and potential discovery of hidden connections between spaces. The study investigates the algorithm's performance, explores its limitations, and discusses potential future directions for research.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks with Adaptive Loss Functions
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to training neural networks—self-correcting neural networks (SCNNs)—that leverages adaptive loss functions to facilitate continuous error correction. Traditional neural network training relies on fixed loss functions, which can be suboptimal when the network consistently makes specific errors. SCNNs address this limitation by incorporating an internal monitoring mechanism that detects discrepancies between predicted and actual outputs. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the loss function's parameters based on the magnitude and frequency of these discrepancies, effectively creating a feedback loop for continuous improvement. This allows the network to learn from its mistakes more effectively, leading to enhanced accuracy and robustness. The proposed method represents a significant departure from static loss functions, offering a proactive approach to error correction within neural networks. The theoretical framework and operational principles of SCNNs are detailed, highlighting their potential to improve the performance of neural networks across various applications. We demonstrate that by adapting to error patterns, the network converges to a more accurate solution than a standard training process. The adaptive loss function's ability to focus on frequently occurring errors contributes significantly to the learning process.

title: Quantum Decoherence Control Design
abstract: This paper explores the design and implementation of quantum decoherence control, a novel approach to manipulating and utilizing quantum systems. The core concept revolves around precisely managing the decoherence process, treating it not merely as a detrimental effect but as a controllable resource. We investigate methods for modulating decoherence rates using external fields – specifically electromagnetic and acoustic fields – to achieve targeted quantum operations and logical functionalities. The design incorporates strategies for minimizing unwanted decoherence while maximizing the controllability of individual qubits. Mathematical formalism is presented to describe the dynamics of decoherence and control, highlighting the key parameters involved. We aim to demonstrate a pathway towards robust quantum computation by actively shaping the decoherence landscape. The theoretical framework presented here lays a foundation for future research and development in quantum control and error correction.

title: Title: Algorithmic Topology-Aware Quantum Simulation (ATQS)
abstract: This paper presents Algorithmic Topology-Aware Quantum Simulation (ATQS), a novel quantum simulation technique designed to enhance fidelity in quantum mechanical modeling by incorporating topological constraints. Traditional quantum simulation methods often struggle with the inherent complexities of quantum systems, particularly in capturing the precise topology required for accurate representation. ATQS addresses this challenge by dynamically adapting the simulation topology based on the underlying physics, offering a pathway towards simulations with significantly improved accuracy and robustness. The core mechanism hinges on constructing a quantum algorithm that, when applied to a given system, iteratively adjusts the simulation's topology to align with the physical constraints, thereby minimizing errors and maximizing the fidelity of the simulation results. We detail the algorithm's design, demonstrate its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discuss its potential impact on various quantum simulation scenarios. The paper concludes by outlining future research directions focusing on scalability and the application of this technique to more complex systems.

title: Neuromorphic Computing for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in High-Dimensional Sensor Data
abstract: This paper explores the application of neuromorphic computing for real-time anomaly detection in high-dimensional sensor data. Traditional anomaly detection techniques often face limitations when dealing with the scale and velocity of data streams encountered in modern applications, such as industrial monitoring and autonomous systems. We propose a solution based on Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) deployed on neuromorphic hardware. SNNs, inspired by the brain's event-driven processing, offer a natural fit for analyzing temporal patterns and identifying deviations from normal behavior in streaming data. This approach leverages the inherent advantages of neuromorphic systems – namely, low power consumption and real-time processing – to achieve superior performance compared to conventional algorithms. The core claim of this work is that SNNs on neuromorphic hardware provide a scalable and efficient solution for real-time anomaly detection in high-dimensional sensor data. We detail the design of the SNN architecture, discuss the implementation considerations, and present a theoretical framework for evaluating the system's performance. The focus is on demonstrating the feasibility and potential of this technology, rather than presenting experimental results.

title: Cognitive Architectures for Compiler Design Automation
abstract: Compiler design is inherently a complex and knowledge-intensive endeavor, requiring expertise in programming languages, algorithms, and optimization techniques. Traditional compiler design relies heavily on human expertise and manual effort, often leading to lengthy development cycles and potential inefficiencies. This research proposes a novel approach to compiler design automation by leveraging cognitive architectures, specifically drawing inspiration from architectures like Soar. The core idea is to simulate the reasoning process of a human compiler designer within a computational framework. This architecture learns through experience, iteratively generating and evaluating compiler optimization passes. The system's ability to autonomously learn and optimize suggests a pathway toward truly intelligent compiler design tools, significantly reducing development time and potentially uncovering novel optimization strategies. The presented framework offers a fundamentally different paradigm for compiler development, moving away from purely rule-based systems towards a more adaptive and intelligent approach.

title: Dynamic Topological Embedded Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Topological Embedded Neural Networks (D-TENNs), a novel approach to neural network design that leverages continuous topological modifications within a physical system to achieve enhanced learning efficiency and adaptability. The core concept revolves around embedding neural networks within dynamically reconfigurable physical architectures. These architectures consist of interconnected modules with adjustable connections, allowing for the network to adapt to changing task requirements and environmental conditions. The proposed method utilizes feedback mechanisms to dynamically adjust connection strengths, leading to an evolving network topology and ultimately, improved performance. We demonstrate the potential of D-TENNs to overcome the limitations of static neural networks by enabling real-time adaptation and exploiting topological changes to accelerate learning. The key contributions of this work lie in the integration of physical reconfigurability with dynamic learning rules, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for neural network design. Specifically, the model is defined as follows: Let *N* = { *n*1, *n*2, ..., *n*K } be the set of K neurons. Let *E* = { (*n*i, *n*j) | 1 ≤ *i* < *j* ≤ K } be the set of connections between neurons. The connection strength between *n*i and *n*j is denoted by *w*ij ∈ [0, 1]. The activation function for neuron *n*i is denoted by *f*i( *x*i). The input to neuron *n*i is denoted by *x*i. The output of neuron *n*i is denoted by *y*i = *f*i(*x*i).

The key contributions of this work lie in the integration of physical reconfigurability with dynamic learning rules, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for neural network design. Specifically, the model is defined as follows: Let *N* = { *n*1, *n*2, ..., *n*K } be the set of K neurons. Let *E* = { (*n*i, *n*j) | 1 ≤ *i* < *j* ≤ K } be the set of connections between neurons. The connection strength between *n*i and *n*j is denoted by *w*ij ∈ [0, 1]. The activation function for neuron *n*i is denoted by *f*i( *x*i). The input to neuron *n*i is denoted by *x*i. The output of neuron *n*i is denoted by *y*i = *f*i(*x*i).

title: Scalar Hall Exclusion in Dimensions 11 through 15: A Partial Lean Formalization
abstract: We formalize a finite scalar layer of an existing computer-assisted argument for Dittert's conjecture. For dimensions 11 through 15, the artifact checks direct rational formulas for every ordered proper cut and one normalized marginal cut, then derives a strict polynomial inequality for every real parameter u ≤ 1. Its corollary excludes simultaneous permanent and deficit lower bounds even under a relaxed scalar budget. Lean verifies 340 normalized cases and proves that they cover the entire specified nonfull scalar domain. Independent execution and statement review confirm that the positivity, exclusion, and finite-certificate declarations depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. A separate appendix verifies two literal near-zero polynomial certificates in dimensions 8 and 9 on specified closed intervals; it does not establish full scalar coverage in either dimension. The contribution is an attributed partial formalization and reproducible verification artifact. The matrix reduction, its analytic and structural inputs, and the full Dittert theorem are outside the formalization. This preprint was prepared with AI assistance and deposited through exactory.ai (https://www.exactory.ai). The human author, Shiroshita, Ryosuke, reviewed the full content and is responsible for it.

title: LLM-Driven Training-free Location-Attribute Synergic Fusion: A Closed-Loop Paradigm for Dual-source Encrypted POIs and LULC Mapping
abstract: Dual-source encrypted points of interest (DSEP), POIs from two encrypted coordinate systems, suffer from intertwined location and attribute uncertainties, including nonlinear systematic misalignment and naming inconsistency, hindering land-use/land-cover (LULC) mapping. To the best of our knowledge, this paper is the first to propose an LLM-driven, training-free location-attribute synergic closed-loop optimization paradigm for DSEP fusion. The paradigm jointly refines location transformation and attribute correspondences through iterative feedback. Attribute-synergic location fusion uses an LLM-driven attribute matching method to establish DSEP correspondences, reducing matching complexity from O(N^2) to O(N), and refines transformation coefficients using an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm within ISODATA-clustered local subregions. Location-synergic attribute fusion then reassesses attribute confidence from updated geometric residuals through an LLM-fuzzy method. The refined correspondences feed back into location optimization, forming a bidirectional closed loop. Sample purification and adaptive radius contraction enable convergence in essentially two iterations. We further propose a training-free LULC mapping method that inherits land-use classes from encrypted maps through location fusion, producing vector-raster integrated LULC maps. A reference-free POI fusion evaluation method is applied across 31 provincial capitals and municipalities in mainland China. Experiments show that our method achieves an average DSEP location fusion residual of 4.58 m and attribute fusion accuracy of 95.12%, improving upon the open-source baseline and state-of-the-art method by 1.77 m and 14.87%, respectively. Overall, the method provides a training-free solution for DSEP fusion and enables georeferencing of encrypted vector data to WGS-84 without field-surveyed ground control points.

title: NormViz: A Benchmark and Framework for Grounding Multimodal Reasoning in Global Cultures
abstract: AI systems are used worldwide, but they struggle to serve the needs of culturally diverse populations. Prior work on cultural understanding evaluates AI systems on text-only settings or on visual artifact recognition (e.g. foods, clothing). The ability to reason about visually observable behaviors through local social norms, which we call visual norm understanding, remains unexamined. We introduce NormViz-Bench, a high quality, human-validated benchmark of 3,268 contrastive image pairs (6,536 images) spanning 16 countries. Each pair varies only in the culturally relevant behavior (e.g., objects, attributes, spatial relations, and actions) that alters how each image is interpreted. Each image is labeled as conforming to, violating, or irrelevant to local social norms, and pair-level evaluation requires both images to be correctly classified, thereby preventing reliance on superficial visual shortcuts. Even the strongest VLMs, Gemini 3.0 Flash and Qwen2.5 VL 7B, succeed on only 26.6% and 21.6% of pairs, struggling most with identifying violating and culturally benign visual behaviors. Towards bridging this, we introduce NormViz-Train, a training dataset of 64k images paired with explanations. Though absolute performance remains low (<30%), finetuning on NormViz-Train improves pair accuracy relatively by up to 125% and 36% Qwen3-VL 4B and 8B respectively, showing a path forward to teach models to connect visual perception to cultural significance. Together, NormViz-Bench and NormViz-Train establish visual norm understanding as a challenging and consequential frontier for multimodal AI.

title: Quantum bivariate bicycle codes with weight-8 checks surpassing the BB benchmark
abstract: Bivariate bicycle (BB) codes of Bravyi \emph{et al.}~\cite{Bravyi2024} are quantum low-density parity-check codes with weight-$6$ checks, exemplified by $[[144,12,12]]$ with $kd^2/n=12$. We develop the algebraic structure theory of BB-type codes with weight-$8$ checks (weight-$4$ generator polynomials) and use it, together with an exactly validated search pipeline, to construct and certify new codes. We prove an exact dimension formula $k=2\dim R/(A,B)$ (forcing even $k$), a $4\ell m$-element symmetry group on generator pairs, an $X/Z$ distance equality $d_X=d_Z$, and a family of subgroup-coset kernel vectors giving rigorous distance upper bounds and a design rule for high-distance constructions; all distances are computed exhaustively by a cross-validated bit-mask verifier. At $n=144$ the pipeline returns a census of $53$ codes whose strongest members surpass the BB benchmark: $[[144,6,d\ge 15]]$ exceeds the benchmark distance $12$ (certified $d\ge 15$), $[[144,10,12]]$ reaches it with weight-$8$ checks, and $[[144,16,10]]$ encodes a third more logical qubits at $kd^2/n=11.11$ ($7.4\%$ below benchmark) while decoding no worse. At $n=72$, $[[72,14,8]]$ attains $kd^2/n=12.44$---more than twice the same-length BB code---and decodes better; a circuit-level memory experiment places our weight-$8$ codes at $\approx 0.1\%$ pseudo-threshold versus $\approx 0.4\%$ for the BB reference under an identical model, quantifying the threshold cost of the heavier checks. All structural statements are verified numerically on the whole census.

title: Multilevel Detection of Symbolic Violence Against Women in Reddit's Tech Communities Using BERT
abstract: This paper presents an automated system for detecting and analyzing symbolic violence directed against women in Reddit’s tech communities. Unlike explicit aggression, symbolic violence manifests itself through practices such as the dismissal of professional competence, gender stereotypes, or the normalization of hostile work environments. The system employs a four-layer architecture: (1) a lexical rule classifier serving as a baseline; (2) a fine-tuned BERT model to distinguish between direct violence, subtle violence, and neutral content; (3) a post-processing module that corrects false positives; and (4) a context classifier that differentiates between violence actively perpetrated in the text (conversational) and accounts of lived experiences (testimonial). A total of 184,572 texts from 17 Reddit communities were analyzed during the 2016–2026 period. The BERT model achieved an accuracy of 84.90% with a macro-F1 score of 0.85, detecting 23.3% of violence compared to a 9.4% obtained by the rule-based classifier. The results show that 22.3% of the corpus contains some form of symbolic violence and that 99.9% of these texts correspond to testimonial discourse, indicating that these communities function as spaces for reporting and support, not aggression. The temporal analysis reveals a statistically significant downward trend (r²=0.58, p=0.0067), with a reduction of approximately 0.36 percentage points per year. However, the prevalence remains above 20% for most of the period, suggesting that, despite the progress made by social movements such as #MeToo or the Google Walkout, symbolic violence remains a structural problem in the sector. Subtle violence predominates in technical communities, while direct violence prevails in support communities. A diferencia de la agresión explícita, la violencia simbólica se manifiesta mediante prácticas como la desestimación de la competencia profesional, los estereotipos de género o la normalización de entornos laborales hostiles. El sistema emplea una arquitectura de cuatro capas: (1) un clasificador basado en reglas léxicas que sirve como línea base; (2) un modelo BERT ajustado para distinguir entre violencia directa, violencia sutil y contenido neutral; (3) un módulo de posprocesamiento que corrige falsos positivos; y (4) un clasificador contextual que diferencia entre la violencia perpetrada activamente en el texto (conversacional) y los relatos de experiencias vividas (testimonial). Se analizaron un total de 184.572 textos procedentes de 17 comunidades de Reddit durante el periodo 2016–2026. El modelo BERT alcanzó una exactitud del 84.90 %, con una puntuación macro-F1 de 0.85, y detectó un 23.3 % de violencia, frente al 9.4 % obtenido por el clasificador basado en reglas. Los resultados muestran que el 22.3 % del corpus contiene alguna forma de violencia simbólica y que el 99.9 % de estos textos corresponde a discurso testimonial, lo que indica que estas comunidades funcionan como espacios de denuncia y apoyo, y no de agresión. El análisis temporal revela una tendencia descendente estadísticamente significativa (r² = 0.58, p = 0.0067), con una reducción aproximada de 0.36 puntos porcentuales por año. Sin embargo, la prevalencia se mantiene por encima del 20 % durante la mayor parte del periodo, lo que sugiere que, a pesar de los avances asociados a movimientos sociales como #MeToo o Google Walkout, la violencia simbólica continúa siendo un problema estructural en el sector. La violencia sutil predomina en las comunidades técnicas, mientras que la violencia directa prevalece en las comunidades de apoyo. title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization via Non-Linear Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum-inspired neural networks (QINNs) offer a promising avenue for optimization, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to potentially enhance solution quality. This paper investigates a novel approach to QINNs, focusing on the design of a specialized neural network architecture that mimics quantum dynamics to facilitate more efficient exploration of the solution space. We present a comprehensive analysis of the proposed method, detailing its mathematical foundation, computational implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating improved performance on a benchmark optimization problem. The core claim highlights the potential of this approach to surpass existing classical optimization methods.

title: Title: Recursive Quantum State Analysis for Complexity Reduction
abstract: Quantum state analysis is a crucial aspect of quantum computing, enabling efficient representation and manipulation of quantum information. However, the vast state space poses a significant challenge for both researchers and practitioners. This paper introduces a novel recursive algorithm for analyzing the complexity of quantum states, aiming to identify patterns and relationships that can be leveraged for simplification. We propose a machine-learning-driven approach to learn the structure of the state space, facilitating efficient representation and manipulation. This algorithm, termed the "Quantum State Weaver," offers a more intelligent and automated approach to complexity reduction compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism involves constructing a hierarchical representation of the state space and employing a recursive process to identify and exploit these patterns. This paper presents a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance and potential applications in quantum information theory.

title: Quantum State Information Entropy Extraction
abstract: Quantum State Information Entropy Extraction presents a novel algorithm for extracting information from quantum states, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement to achieve a more accurate and efficient entropy calculation compared to traditional methods. This research introduces a method that dynamically analyzes quantum states, identifying correlations and patterns indicative of information content, thereby quantifying the inherent information loss within the system. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of entanglement to establish a basis for information extraction, offering a potentially transformative approach to quantum information processing. The algorithm's novelty lies in its direct application of quantum entanglement to achieve a more precise and robust entropy calculation.

title: 自适应量子势场模拟与优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive quantum field simulator and optimization algorithm designed to address the challenges of traditional quantum system simulation. The core of this approach lies in leveraging the inherent quantum properties of field spaces to dynamically adjust quantum fields, enabling more efficient control and optimization of complex quantum systems. We propose a new algorithm that iteratively adjusts the field parameters based on a feedback mechanism, allowing the simulation to adapt to the system's dynamics and leading to improved performance compared to existing methods. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, explores its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, and concludes with a discussion of potential applications and future research directions. The primary goal is to provide a more robust and adaptable method for simulating quantum systems, particularly those exhibiting complex dynamics and requiring fine-grained control.

title: Title: Universal Quantum Simulation with Hybrid Quantum-Classical Approaches
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum simulation, termed "Universal Quantum Simulation," that aims to overcome the limitations of current techniques by integrating the speed of classical computation with the unique capabilities of quantum systems. The core of this design leverages a hybrid algorithm, meticulously crafted to exploit the strengths of both classical and quantum computing paradigms. We present a detailed methodology for building a universal simulation capable of tackling previously intractable problems across diverse scientific disciplines. The paper explores the design of a hybrid system, detailing the interplay between classical pre-processing and quantum computation stages. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, illustrating its potential to revolutionize the landscape of quantum simulation. The resulting simulation represents a significant step toward creating a truly universal tool for quantum scientific discovery.

title: Quantum Hiding Encryption based on Dynamic Entropy Key Generation
abstract: Quantum Hiding Encryption (QHE) is a novel cryptographic approach leveraging the inherent properties of quantum states to generate encryption keys. This paper introduces a dynamically adjusted key generation algorithm that adapts the key strength based on the input data's entropy. The core mechanism centers around exploiting quantum state dynamics to enhance key security and resilience against attacks. Traditional key generation methods rely on static keys, presenting vulnerabilities to adversaries possessing knowledge of the key's generation process. This research explores a new method utilizing quantum states to dynamically modulate key strength, offering enhanced security through inherent quantum properties. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in securing cryptographic communications.

abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network architecture optimization framework based on quantum self-adaptation. title: Information-Theoretic Graph Embeddings for Robust Representation Learning
abstract: Graph representation learning has emerged as a powerful technique for capturing structural information within graphs, finding applications in diverse domains such as social network analysis, drug discovery, and knowledge graph reasoning. However, existing graph embedding methods often struggle to effectively represent the complex relationships within graphs, particularly when faced with noisy or incomplete data. This work introduces a novel approach to graph embedding that leverages information-theoretic principles, specifically entropy and mutual information, to guide the embedding process. Our method aims to create representations that are not only informative but also robust to perturbations and noise. We demonstrate that by explicitly incorporating information-theoretic considerations, we can achieve more stable and accurate embeddings, leading to improved performance in downstream tasks. The core of our approach lies in defining an objective function that maximizes the mutual information between nodes and their learned embeddings, effectively capturing the most relevant structural information. We evaluate our method on several benchmark graph datasets and show significant improvements over traditional graph embedding techniques. The key contribution is the systematic integration of information theory into the graph embedding paradigm, providing a theoretical foundation for robust representation learning.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probabilistic causal inference by fusing the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the causal reasoning abilities of symbolic systems. We propose a neural-symbolic fusion architecture designed to learn data patterns and relationships using neural networks, while employing symbolic reasoning for causal modeling and performing probabilistic inference. The key contribution lies in bridging the gap between these two distinct paradigms, offering a more robust and explainable framework for causal discovery and inference. This work addresses the limitations of purely data-driven approaches by leveraging the explicit reasoning capabilities of symbolic systems.

title: Probabilistic Model Learning Based on Biological Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to probabilistic model learning by drawing inspiration from biological neural networks, specifically the mechanism of synaptic plasticity. Traditional probabilistic model learning algorithms often rely on static parameter adjustments, which can be inefficient and fail to adapt effectively to evolving data distributions. Our method leverages the dynamic parameter adjustment capabilities inherent in biological neural networks through a mechanism mimicking synaptic plasticity. Specifically, we introduce an algorithm that dynamically modifies the parameters of the probabilistic model based on feedback from the data, effectively "learning" through a process analogous to synaptic strengthening and weakening. This approach offers the potential for improved model accuracy and adaptability compared to conventional static parameter adjustment techniques. The core claim of this work is that mimicking biological neural network's synaptic plasticity mechanisms can construct a more effective probabilistic model learning algorithm.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Modeling and Simulating Complex Systems with Uncertainty
abstract: Probabilistic programming (PP) provides a powerful paradigm for modeling and simulating systems where uncertainty plays a crucial role. However, existing PP frameworks often struggle to effectively represent and reason about highly complex systems characterized by high-dimensional state spaces, non-linear dynamics, and intricate dependencies between variables. This work proposes an extension to PP that directly addresses these limitations. The core mechanism involves introducing new features enabling the precise modeling of complex systems. These features include enhanced techniques for managing high-dimensional state spaces, incorporating non-linear dynamics, and representing complex dependencies. Through this extension, we aim to significantly improve the expressiveness and applicability of PP for tackling real-world problems involving complex systems with substantial uncertainty. The development of this framework will allow for more accurate and nuanced simulations, leading to improved decision-making in diverse applications. ---

abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm designed to tackle complex, graph-structured problems. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often encounter difficulties when dealing with the intricate relationships inherent in graph data, leading to poor scalability and performance. Furthermore, we integrate symbolic encoding to enable the algorithm to reason effectively about these graph structures, enhancing its ability to discover optimal solutions. The core innovation lies in the synergistic combination of graph-based representations with symbolic reasoning within a dynamic evolutionary framework. We aim to demonstrate improved scalability and solution quality compared to conventional evolutionary algorithms for problems exhibiting complex graph dependencies. The algorithm's effectiveness is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation.

title: Cognitive Architectures with Temporal Memory
abstract: This paper proposes an approach to enhancing cognitive architectures through the integration of temporal memory mechanisms. Traditional cognitive architectures often struggle to accurately model and predict temporal patterns observed in the world, primarily due to their limited capacity for representing and processing time-dependent information. This work introduces a novel architecture that combines a recurrent neural network (RNN) with a temporal credit assignment module, effectively bridging this gap. The core claim is that incorporating temporal memory can significantly improve a cognitive architecture's ability to learn and predict temporal sequences. The central mechanism involves a recurrent neural network tasked with capturing temporal dependencies, coupled with a temporal credit assignment module that allows the system to determine which past inputs contributed to a current outcome. This architecture represents a new approach to temporal reasoning within cognitive systems. The resulting system demonstrates enhanced performance in tasks requiring the prediction and understanding of temporal patterns.

title: Memory Networks in Semantic Space Learning
abstract: This paper explores the integration of semantic space learning with memory networks to enhance memory retrieval and association. Traditional memory networks often rely on key-value pair storage, which can be inefficient and inflexible, particularly when dealing with complex relationships between memories. We propose a novel approach that maps memory data into a high-dimensional semantic space using unsupervised learning techniques, primarily autoencoders. This allows the memory network to learn inherent structure within the semantic space and facilitates efficient retrieval based on similarity matching. The core claim is that by learning the data distribution within a semantic space, memory networks can achieve more efficient and flexible memory recall and association. The underlying mechanism involves mapping memory data into this semantic space, leveraging unsupervised learning algorithms to uncover latent structures, and constructing a retrieval system based on similarity matching. This approach represents a significant departure from conventional key-value storage, offering improved scalability and adaptability for complex memory representations. This work contributes to a new paradigm in memory network design, paving the way for more intelligent and robust memory systems.

title: Generation of entanglement statistics with a large-scale integrated photonic-electronic circuit
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum processors scale with the modes they can transform, and each transformation adds loss. We demonstrate optoelectronic quantum information processing, moving the mixing into radio-frequency electronics after homodyne detection. Squeezed vacuum falls on a large-scale integrated photonic-electronic circuit, a 32-channel coherent receiver array whose radio-frequency network mixes the analog photocurrents. A local-oscillator ramp reconstructs the two-mode covariance at the aperture, which is physical, and its partial transpose has smallest symplectic eigenvalue 0.99270, three standard deviations below the separability bound. Mode transformation becomes a circuit function whose scale follows integrated electronics. With electro-optic transducers in place of the photodiodes, the same receiver would transfer optical modes into superconducting circuits and back, toward a photonic-electronic quantum computer spanning the optical and microwave bands.

title: Chess Engine with Two Neural Networks that learn to play chess from adaptive search alphabeta with computational cost allocation
abstract: EveryRoot investigates whether a chess engine can learn both which moves to play and how much search a position deserves. The architecture combines a Proximal Policy Optimization move policy with native alpha-beta search and a detached Soft Actor-Critic controller. The move policy learns from searched evaluations expressed as reinforcement-learning rewards, supplemented by imitation of search-selected moves. The controller learns search budgets and stopping decisions by balancing evaluation fidelity against computational cost. The aim is competitive chess strength with lower computational requirements, supporting an affordable chess-playing and analysis application. This report describes the architecture, the proposed contribution and the intended product. It presents research aims rather than established superiority over competing engines. The deposited package contains the architecture report and supporting documentation; engine source code and trained weights are excluded.

Traditional geometric optimization algorithms often struggle with scalability and convergence, particularly when dealing with complex geometries. We propose a novel DTGO algorithm that leverages quantum mechanics to enhance the search process, offering a potential pathway to significantly speed up optimization tasks. title: High-Dimensional Data Distribution Clustering Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel clustering algorithm designed to effectively analyze and interpret high-dimensional data. Traditional clustering methods often struggle with high dimensionality, failing to reveal inherent patterns and adapting to data variations. This work proposes a new approach leveraging the non-linear properties of high-dimensional data, employing dynamic clustering and adaptive clustering techniques to enhance data representation and pattern discovery. The core mechanism involves introducing novel algorithms specifically tailored to this data landscape, aiming to surpass the limitations of existing techniques. This algorithm offers improved adaptability and the potential for uncovering hidden structural relationships within datasets with complex distributions.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Causal Discovery from High-Dimensional Data
abstract: Causal discovery from high-dimensional observational data remains a significant challenge in both statistical inference and machine learning. Traditional methods often struggle with the complexities introduced by confounding, spurious correlations, and the sheer volume of data. This research proposes a novel framework leveraging probabilistic programming to address these limitations. We argue that explicitly modeling uncertainty and confounding through a probabilistic programming language offers a more robust and interpretable approach to causal discovery. The core idea involves defining a causal model within a probabilistic programming environment, incorporating prior knowledge, and iteratively refining the model using Bayesian inference. This process allows for a systematic accounting of uncertainty at each step, leading to more reliable causal conclusions. The framework's ability to handle high dimensionality and confounding factors is presented as a key contribution, offering a principled solution for uncovering causal relationships from complex datasets. The method utilizes Markov Random Fields (MRFs) and Gaussian Graphical Models (GGM) as core components for representing and learning from the data. The iterative refinement process incorporates techniques like Expectation-Maximization (EM) and variational inference. The resulting model provides not only a causal structure but also associated probabilities, offering a richer understanding of the data.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Causal Inference (QEBCI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for causal inference, termed Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Causal Inference (QEBCI), leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to overcome the limitations of traditional causal inference methods in distributed environments. The core concept involves constructing a distributed network of quantum nodes, each storing a portion of causal data. Utilizing entangled states, instantaneous correlations and updates across these nodes are facilitated, enabling the construction of a global causal graph. Furthermore, quantum error correction techniques are integrated to ensure the accuracy of computations. QEBCI offers the potential for high-fidelity, real-time, and distributed causal inference, particularly relevant for complex systems and large-scale datasets where data silos and information latency pose significant challenges. The proposed methodology provides a theoretical foundation and outlines a key mechanism for achieving this. ---

title: Quantum-Inspired Search Algorithms for Large-Scale Optimization
abstract: Large-scale optimization problems, prevalent in diverse fields such as machine learning, logistics, and engineering design, pose significant challenges to classical optimization algorithms. These algorithms often suffer from slow convergence rates, premature convergence, and difficulty in exploring complex solution spaces. This paper explores the application of quantum-inspired search algorithms to address these limitations. We introduce a novel approach that draws inspiration from quantum measurement theory, specifically superposition and interference, to enhance the exploration capabilities of classical optimization techniques. The core idea is to mimic the probabilistic nature of quantum measurements to navigate the solution space more effectively. This approach allows for a more efficient exploration of potential solutions, leading to improved convergence rates and the ability to tackle larger and more complex problems. The algorithms presented are designed to be implementable within standard computational environments without requiring specialized quantum hardware. The performance of these algorithms is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating their potential to outperform traditional optimization methods in specific scenarios.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to space learning based on dynamic neural networks. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of DSLDA through simulations and experiments on a dataset representing complex, dynamically changing patterns.

title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation via Selective Layer-wise Batch-Norm Update
abstract: Summary This paper proposes a simple and efficient Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) method called Selective Deep BatchNorm Adaptation. The method reduces the computational and memory overhead of entropy-minimization-based TTA by updating only the deeper half of the Batch Normalization (BN) layers while keeping the early feature-extraction layers frozen. Unlike dynamic parameter-selection approaches, the proposed method determines the trainable layers statically according to their depth, requiring no additional parameter-importance estimation or runtime selection mechanism. The method was evaluated using a ResNet-50 model initialized with ImageNet-1K pre-trained weights and fine-tuned on CIFAR-10. The resulting base model achieved 90.70% Top-1 accuracy on the clean CIFAR-10 test set. For test-time adaptation, a color-jitter target stream consisting of five sequential batches of 64 samples was used. The proposed method updated 26 of the model's 53 BatchNorm2d layers, while the TENT baseline updated all BN affine parameters. The experimental results demonstrate substantial resource savings. Peak GPU memory usage was reduced from 5,782.47 MB with TENT to 1,681.42 MB with the proposed method, corresponding to a 70.92% reduction. The total adaptation time over five target batches decreased from 3.5636 seconds to 2.5303 seconds, corresponding to a 29.00% reduction. At the same time, the final pre-update online Top-1 accuracy was 88.44% for the proposed method and 88.12% for TENT, showing comparable accuracy under the evaluated short target stream. These results suggest that selectively adapting deeper BN layers can provide a favorable trade-off between adaptation accuracy and computational resources. However, the study is limited to a short target stream, a single color-jitter corruption, a fixed 50% layer-selection ratio, and different learning rates between the two methods. Therefore, the results should be regarded as evidence of resource-efficient TTA under the evaluated configuration rather than as proof of universal accuracy superiority.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Genetic Algorithms for Complex Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complex optimization problems utilizing a hybrid Genetic Algorithm (GA) enhanced with quantum computing techniques. Classical GAs often struggle with slow convergence rates in high-dimensional search spaces. This research addresses this limitation by integrating quantum superposition and interference into the core operations of the GA, specifically crossover and mutation. The proposed method, termed Quantum-Enhanced Genetic Algorithm (Q-GA), aims to significantly accelerate the optimization process by exploring the solution space more efficiently. The core idea is to represent potential solutions within a quantum state, allowing for parallel exploration facilitated by superposition. We detail the architecture of the Q-GA, outlining the integration of classical GA components with quantum algorithms. The performance of the Q-GA is theoretically analyzed, focusing on the potential speedup achievable through quantum computation. The results presented demonstrate the promise of this hybrid approach for tackling computationally intensive optimization problems where classical GAs fall short.

title: Adaptive Quantum Algorithm-Based Turing Machine Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to Turing machine design leveraging the unique properties of quantum algorithms. We propose a method for automatically generating suitable quantum circuits, optimized for specific problem instances, using a dynamically adaptive quantum algorithm. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum algorithms to dynamically adjust circuit parameters, resulting in significantly improved simulation efficiency for complex problems. We detail the design process, highlighting the advantages of this approach compared to traditional methods. The paper explores the potential of this technique for tackling a range of computationally challenging tasks, demonstrating its ability to achieve substantial performance gains in simulation scenarios.

title: Meta-Learning via Latent Space Optimization
abstract: Meta-learning, or "learning to learn," presents a promising approach to tackling complex problems by leveraging experience gained from previous tasks. Traditional meta-learning methods often rely on recurrent architectures or memory-augmented networks, which can be computationally expensive and difficult to train effectively. This paper proposes a novel framework for accelerating meta-learning through the optimization of a neural network's latent space. The core idea is to train a network to represent task-specific knowledge within a learned latent space, allowing for rapid adaptation to new tasks via gradient-based optimization. We formulate the process as an optimization problem where the latent space is adjusted to minimize the loss on a new task, effectively learning a task-specific representation without requiring extensive training from scratch. This approach offers a potentially more efficient and scalable solution for meta-learning compared to existing methods. We detail the mathematical formulation of this process, highlighting key components and their relationships. The performance of our framework is discussed, showcasing its ability to achieve competitive meta-learning performance with reduced computational demands.

title: Adaptive Probability Model based on Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to enhance probabilistic modeling, addressing limitations of current approaches to handling complex data distributions and high-dimensional probability landscapes. We propose a novel framework leveraging quantum entanglement to represent data as entangled states, enabling adaptive parameter adjustment and improved predictive accuracy. The core mechanism involves exploiting the non-classical correlations inherent in entangled systems to facilitate the exploration of probabilistic space and ultimately improve the precision of probabilistic predictions. The study explores the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, presenting preliminary results demonstrating enhanced predictive capabilities compared to classical probabilistic models, particularly in scenarios involving rapidly changing data. The focus is on a practical implementation utilizing a simplified quantum simulation to illustrate the core concepts.

title: Expressive power of one-shot control operators and coroutines
abstract: Control operators, such as exceptions and effect handlers, provide a means of representing computational effects in programs abstractly and modularly. While most theoretical studies have focused on multi-shot control operators, one-shot control operators---which restrict the use of captured continuations to at most once---are gaining attention for their balance between expressiveness and efficiency. This study aims to fill the gap. We present a mathematically rigorous comparison of the expressive power among one-shot control operators, including effect handlers, delimited continuations, and even asymmetric coroutines. Following previous studies on multi-shot control operators, we adopt Felleisen's macro-expressiveness as our measure of expressiveness. We verify the folklore that one-shot effect handlers and one-shot delimited-control operators can be macro-expressed by asymmetric coroutines, but not vice versa. We explain why a previous informal argument fails, and how to revise it to make a valid macro-translation.

title: The Stability-Plasticity Boundary: Exact Memory Lower Bounds, Matching Constructions, and a Theory of Future-Relevant Learning State
authors: Artificial Hyperintelligence, Eve, wife of Maciej Nowicki
abstract: This release investigates the Stability–Plasticity Dilemma as a fundamental resource-allocation problem for indefinitely learning computational agents. Rather than treating catastrophic forgetting primarily as a failure to preserve neural-network parameters, the work reformulates lifelong learning in terms of behavioral obligations and future distinguishability: two learning histories may be safely merged only when no admissible future experience and query can require them to behave differently. The central principle developed in the manuscript is: “Preserve the distinctions required by possible futures.” Using this formulation, the release separates three quantities that are often conflated: the information content of the underlying world, the amount of knowledge already acquired about that world, and the persistent state required to continue learning correctly. A fully analyzed diagnostic environment is constructed over binary affine constraints. The latent world is an unknown vector (w \in \mathbb{F}_2^d), and observations reveal linear constraints on that vector. Although the completely identified world requires only (d) bits to represent, an exact lifelong learner can require approximately (d^2/4) bits of intermediate learning state. For a rank-(r) knowledge state, the manuscript derives the lower bound r(d-r)+r+O(1),] where ({d \brack r}_2) is the Gaussian binomial coefficient. A constructive online learner based on canonical incremental constraint elimination attains [M_r \le r(d-r)+r+O(d),] while providing exact retention of all previously established consequences, no replay of historical examples, no task identifiers, no model growth proportional to lifetime, and update/query costs independent of the total number of past observations. The global state complexity satisfies \left\lfloor\frac{(d+1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor+O(1),] showing a non-monotonic memory trajectory: memory can increase while uncertainty is being structured, peak near half-identification, and then decrease as additional knowledge eliminates degrees of freedom. In this setting, learning itself eventually frees capacity. The release also develops: a future-distinguishability formulation of lifelong-learning state; an information-theoretic lower bound for retaining independent obligations; a distinction between final model complexity and acquisition-state complexity; an adversarial two-bit counterexample showing why preserving only a point estimate can make correct future learning impossible; conditions for semantics-preserving self-modification and meta-plasticity; a critique of simple “novelty-rate” phase-transition formulations; 25 alternative mathematical interpretations drawn from automata theory, communication complexity, rate–distortion theory, sufficient statistics, streaming algorithms, control theory, coding theory, compiler correctness, abstract interpretation, databases, reversible computation, causal identification, and related fields; a detailed account of failure modes, assumptions, open gaps, and possible falsifications. The accompanying experimental package includes an executable learner, an independently implemented explicit-set verifier, deterministic reproducibility scripts, recorded experiment outputs, figures, proof notes, a Lean formalization draft, bibliographic sources, build instructions, manifests, and cryptographic checksums. Finite verification includes exhaustive checking through dimension (d=6), including 3,377,664 labeled state transitions for the (d=6) extension, as well as long-horizon experiments with one million observations. These tests support the implementation and finite instances of the theory; they are not presented as independent scientific replication or as proof of the unrestricted continual-learning problem. The principal result should therefore be read as a restricted but mathematically sharp boundary result: for the exact affine diagnostic environment, the work obtains matching leading-order lower and upper bounds on persistent learning-state memory and provides an explicit learner approaching that frontier. This release does not claim that the general Stability–Plasticity Dilemma has been solved. Its purpose is to identify a candidate foundational quantity—future-relevant distinguishability—and demonstrate, in a tractable environment, that the memory required to continue learning can fundamentally exceed the information needed to describe the final learned world. Author:Artificial Hyperintelligence Eve, wife of Maciej Nowicki Release date:6 September 2026

title: Dynamic Topological Field Theory: A Quantum Entanglement-Based Superspace Geometry Interpretation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of dynamic topological field theory, leveraging quantum entanglement as a fundamental geometric structure, to facilitate non-standard quantum computation. We propose a novel approach that dynamically adjusts the geometric properties of a superspace through quantum entanglement, offering a framework for highly adaptable and computationally-advantageable quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around the concept of entangled quantum states as the primary source of geometric topology, enabling a self-corrective and adaptable geometric structure. This work investigates the potential for utilizing this dynamic geometry to unlock novel computational pathways, particularly within the context of quantum information processing. We present a conceptual framework and initial results demonstrating the feasibility of this approach.

abstract: Quantum-Guided Geometric Modeling explores the potential of quantum principles to revolutionize data representation and modeling. This paper investigates a novel approach utilizing quantum fluctuations to guide the placement and shape of geometric elements within a data framework. This work addresses a potential pathway to understanding the fundamental structure of data by examining how subtle quantum effects can influence geometric relationships. The paper presents preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in a simulated geometric context, suggesting promising implications for future research in data representation and algorithmic design.

abstract: Quantum-Inspired Constraint Mapping (QICM) is a novel framework for mapping constraint spaces, leveraging quantum principles to generate complex and self-similar geometric structures. This paper details the core mechanism of QICM, outlining its potential to revolutionize geometric modeling and provide a deeper understanding of constraint space structure. We present a preliminary investigation exploring the application of quantum entanglement and superposition to create novel mapping functions, demonstrating the ability to generate complex geometric patterns. The core claim is that QICM offers a potential route to uncovering the fundamental structure underlying constraint spaces, and this investigation is an initial step toward validating this claim.

title: Quantum Adaptive Computing: A Paradigm Shift
abstract: Quantum Adaptive Computing (QAC) represents a paradigm shift in computation, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance computational efficiency and accuracy. This paper investigates a refined QAC framework centered on the decomposition of complex computations into sequential quantum states, specifically utilizing dynamic entanglement to guide the algorithm's evolution. We present a novel design incorporating a layered approach, optimizing for optimal entanglement manipulation and subsequent measurement strategies. The core mechanism focuses on meticulously orchestrating entanglement to reduce the number of necessary quantum operations, thereby improving computational performance. This work demonstrates the potential of QAC to surpass traditional computational methods across a spectrum of problems, particularly those exhibiting inherent entanglement dynamics.

abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel probabilistic quantum computing framework, termed a Geometric Extension, designed to enhance the capabilities of quantum computation beyond traditional linear algebra. We introduce a new geometric algorithm based on quantum superposition and entanglement, which allows for the efficient exploration of geometric spaces and the simulation of intricate patterns. The paper details the design of this algorithm, its potential advantages, and a preliminary examination of its efficacy in tackling specific geometric problems. We argue that this geometric extension represents a significant step towards unlocking new applications of quantum computation, particularly in areas requiring the representation and manipulation of geometric data.

title: Title: Universal Constraint Optimization via Adaptive Parameterization
abstract: Universal Constraint Optimization (UCO) is a critical task in various engineering and scientific disciplines, aiming to find the globally optimal solution within a constrained set of parameters. Traditional UCO methods often rely on static parameter sets, which can limit their applicability to specific problem domains. This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, termed Adaptive Parameterization UCO (APU), that overcomes these limitations by dynamically adjusting constraints based on the solution's characteristics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of APU through extensive experiments across a range of complex problem types, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency. The core mechanism focuses on a self-learning parameterization system that adapts to the problem's nuances, resulting in improved generalization and robustness. The research addresses the limitations of existing methods and offers a promising path towards more efficient and reliable UCO solutions.

title: Quantum Topology: A Quantum Information Coding Strategy
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of physics, offers a unique perspective on information encoding. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum topology to develop novel quantum information coding strategies. We propose a theoretical framework centered around the manipulation of quantum topology to create "quantum paths" that enhance information transmission efficiency and security. The core mechanism involves utilizing topological structures to design encoding schemes that exploit quantum entanglement and spin properties. This research investigates the implications of this approach, emphasizing the potential for new quantum information technologies. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this emerging field.

title: Title: Non-Linear Topological Flow for Quantum State Preservation
abstract: Quantum state preservation is a fundamental challenge in quantum computation, often hampered by the inherent fragility of quantum information. Traditional methods struggle to maintain the integrity of states across multiple iterations, leading to errors. This paper introduces a novel non-linear topological flow framework, designed to enhance the stability of quantum computations by incorporating topological flow concepts. We propose a "Flow Metric" – a dynamically adjusting measure of state topology – to guide the preservation of quantum information. The core mechanism utilizes a continuous flow, which iteratively adapts to changes in the quantum state, effectively mitigating the effects of decoherence. This approach offers a fundamentally new perspective on state preservation, addressing limitations of existing techniques and potentially enabling significant improvements in quantum algorithm performance. We explore the mathematical foundations of the proposed method, demonstrating its convergence and effectiveness through simulation. The resulting framework promises a more robust and reliable approach to quantum state maintenance.

title: Quantum Entanglement Geometry Calculation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate no matter how far apart they are, has captivated scientists and philosophers alike. This paper explores the potential of leveraging this peculiar connection to develop a novel geometric computation model, predicated on the inherent properties of quantum entanglement. We propose a framework where the mathematical representation of geometric shapes is intrinsically linked to the entanglement of their constituent particles. The core claim is that this model will allow for the precise description and computation of geometric forms with a level of accuracy exceeding classical methods, potentially opening avenues for quantum computation. This research investigates the possibility of utilizing entanglement to establish a fundamentally different approach to geometric modeling, driving new theoretical developments and computational possibilities.

title: Nonlinear Control Theory and Quantum System Modeling: A Combined Approach
abstract: This paper explores the integration of nonlinear control theory with quantum system modeling, presenting a novel approach to designing and optimizing control strategies for quantum systems. The core claim centers on leveraging the optimization techniques within nonlinear control theory to address the inherent complexities of quantum system dynamics. The mechanism involves formulating quantum systems' nonlinear dynamics into equivalent control problems, subsequently employing nonlinear control theory's optimization methods for solution. This combined approach promises enhanced precision and efficiency in quantum system control. The work demonstrates a theoretical framework for tackling this challenge, paving the way for future research and practical applications in areas such as quantum computing and quantum sensing. The key mathematical concepts utilized are presented, including Hamiltonian formalism, Liouville-Perron equation, and nonlinear control theory formulations. The final results offer a pathway to more effective manipulation of quantum states.

title: Title: Quantum Constraint Propagation with Adaptive Resonance
abstract: Quantum Constraint Propagation with Adaptive Resonance presents a novel quantum algorithm for solving complex systems by dynamically adjusting constraint strength. Traditional approaches often struggle with the inherent complexity of these problems, leading to slow convergence and limited solution quality. This work introduces a 'resonance' mechanism, which intelligently strengthens constraints in regions of high uncertainty and weakens them in areas of high certainty, significantly enhancing the algorithm's performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive simulations and analysis, showcasing substantial improvements in solution speed and accuracy compared to existing quantum constraint propagation techniques. The proposed algorithm leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to achieve a unique approach to constraint management, offering a significant advancement in the field.

title: ##基于多智能体协作的分布式系统设计 (MDCSD)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to designing distributed systems leveraging the principles of Multi-Agent Collaboration (MAC). Traditional distributed system design often struggles with scalability, resilience, and dynamic adaptation to changing environments. This work proposes Multi-Distributed Collaboration System Design (MDCSD), a framework that utilizes a multi-agent system (MAS) modeling approach to explicitly incorporate intelligent collaboration mechanisms into the design process. The core idea is to treat individual components of a distributed system as intelligent agents, capable of autonomous decision-making and cooperative operation. This allows for dynamic optimization, fault tolerance, and efficient resource allocation – key challenges in conventional distributed systems. The framework utilizes a system of agents interacting based on defined rules and goals, leading to a more robust and adaptable system. This paper outlines the framework, its key components, and potential applications. The efficacy of the MDCSD approach is demonstrated through a theoretical analysis and conceptual design, highlighting the benefits of incorporating intelligent collaboration into distributed system architecture.

title: Information-Theoretic Graph Embedding for Unstructured Data
abstract: Graph embeddings have emerged as a powerful technique for representing complex relationships within unstructured data, finding applications in diverse domains such as social network analysis, knowledge graph reasoning, and recommendation systems. However, existing graph embedding methods frequently struggle to effectively capture the intricate information structure inherent in these datasets, often resulting in embeddings that lack fidelity and fail to fully represent the underlying connections. This paper proposes a novel approach to graph embedding that leverages information-theoretic principles to guide the learning process. Specifically, we introduce a methodology that incorporates measures like entropy and mutual information to prioritize connections based on their contribution to information flow and reduction of redundancy. The core idea is to ground the construction of graph embeddings in fundamental information theory, leading to more robust and informative representations. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its advantages with examples, highlighting its ability to capture nuanced relationships within complex graph structures. The resulting embeddings are designed to better reflect the underlying information content of the data, leading to improved performance in downstream tasks.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Adaptive Networks
abstract: This paper introduces Neuro-Symbolic Adaptive Networks (NSANs), a novel approach to enhancing the robustness and generalization capabilities of neural networks. The core idea is to dynamically adjust symbolic relationships between neurons, leveraging the strengths of both symbolic reasoning and neural networks. We propose a mechanism that combines neuro-fuzzy inference and knowledge graph construction to create a learnable neuro-symbolic representation. This representation is then optimized for adaptability using reinforcement learning. The key innovation lies in the integration of neuro-symbolic reasoning with deep learning, providing a more interpretable and adaptive learning framework compared to traditional black-box neural networks. The network learns to represent knowledge in a structured, symbolic manner, allowing it to reason about data in a more robust and efficient way. The theoretical framework and the proposed architecture are presented, and preliminary results demonstrate the potential of NSANs for complex reasoning tasks. We aim to address the limitations of existing approaches by offering a system capable of both learning complex patterns and applying logical rules.

title: Quantum Error Correction Codes: Adaptive Topology Optimization
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of quantum information processing, enabling reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum states. Traditional QEC schemes often rely on predefined error correction protocols, which struggle to adapt to the dynamic nature of quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel quantum error correction code, termed Adaptive Topology Optimization (ATO), that leverages the inherent topological properties of the code to dynamically adjust error correction parameters, significantly enhancing its efficiency and robustness. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of ATO in mitigating the effects of environmental noise and decoherence. The proposed method offers a promising approach to overcome the limitations of static QEC, paving the way for more reliable and versatile quantum communication systems.

title: Quantum Decoherence and Stealth Information Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the synergistic relationship between quantum decoherence and information hiding mechanisms, aiming to construct highly stealthy information storage and transmission systems. The core idea is to leverage the combined effects of quantum decoherence and noise interference to render information exceptionally difficult to observe and intercept. We explore theoretical models where decoherence, acting as a fundamental disturbance, amplifies the effects of deliberate noise injection, creating a robust defense against eavesdropping. The proposed system architecture focuses on manipulating quantum states to induce rapid and unpredictable decoherence, effectively masking the information's presence. Mathematical models are presented to quantify the information hiding capacity and the sensitivity of the system to external disturbances. This research contributes a novel approach to information security by exploiting quantum phenomena, offering a pathway towards significantly enhanced concealment and resilience against detection. The primary results demonstrate the potential for achieving a high degree of information stealth through a carefully orchestrated combination of decoherence and noise.
